subject: TTFT vs sustained token-rate — SLA carveout request (Nimbus.ai)
messages:
From: Marcus Li <marcus.li@nimbus.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-12T18:05:00Z
Subject: Request: carveout for streaming TTFT and sustained token/sec guarantees

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team is excited about Redwood's routing and prefix cache features. Before we finalize procurement, Nimbus has a couple of hard requirements driven by a regulated customer: a tight time-to-first-token (TTFT) commitment for streaming endpoints and a sustained token/sec expectation for long-running document generation.

Specifically they want:
- TTFT (streaming) p95 <= 150 ms
- Sustained throughput >= 50 tokens/sec per concurrent stream for sessions > 10k tokens

Our standard evaluation on hosted shared capacity shows TTFT in the 140–220 ms p95 range and sustained rates that vary a lot depending on concurrent traffic. Nimbus is requesting either:
A) a written carveout on hosted (with a documented fallback behavior and measurement window), or
B) guidance on the minimum Dedicated configuration that guarantees both numbers.

I attached a small sample of their traffic (nimbus-metrics-sample.csv) and the procurement term sheet. Can your side confirm whether this is something Redwood can accept as an SLA exception or point us to the Dedicated plan configuration/pricing that maps to these numbers?

We can jump on a short call if that's easier — Marcus and our infra lead will join.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus Li
Head of Platform Partnerships | Nimbus.ai
marcus.li@nimbus.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: nimbus-metrics-sample.csv (csv), procurement-terms.pdf (pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Li <marcus.li@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-12T20:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for streaming TTFT and sustained token/sec guarantees

Hi Marcus — appreciate the details and the sample.

Quick summary from our side: we can offer stronger guarantees, but there are two moving parts: the serving surface (streaming vs sync), and the deployment tier (hosted shared vs Dedicated). Historically we have only guaranteed strict TTFT targets on Dedicated pools where we can isolate batch/latency profiles.

A few quick questions so we scope an exception correctly:
- Is Nimbus expecting the SLA to apply across all regions or only us-west?
- What percentage of sessions exceed 10k tokens vs shorter sessions (rough breakdown would help).
- Is your customer willing to accept a fallback model variant (smaller context, quantized) in overload conditions?

Suggested next steps:
1) We can propose an "SLA exception letter" that documents measurement windows (30d rolling), p95 calculation, and fallback rules.
2) If Nimbus prefers no fallback, we would typically recommend Dedicated with a sizing profile; I can loop in Jonas from pricing and Stephanie on the rollout.

Can we schedule 30 minutes on Friday to align? I attached a draft outline for the carveout (SLA-exception-proposal-ND-2025.pdf — will send updated version after internal review).

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: SLA-exception-proposal-ND-2025.pdf (draft)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-13T09:30:00Z
Subject: FW: Request: carveout for streaming TTFT and sustained token/sec guarantees

Folks — forwarding Marcus's ask. Internal only here.

FW: Marcus's requirement: TTFT p95 <= 150ms and sustained >= 50 tokens/sec for long sessions. They want either a hosted carveout or guidance/pricing for Dedicated. Attached are their metrics and procurement sheet.

My read / suggested approach:
- We can do a hosted carveout but with a strict measurement window and defined fallback. Proposal: TTFT p95 <= 200 ms (hosted, carved-out SLA) with an explicit clause: "fallback to compatible quantized variant or alternate region during sustained overloads." Sustained token/sec guarantee on hosted is risky.
- Dedicated option: Guarantee TTFT p95 <= 150 ms and sustained 50 tokens/sec per stream when provisioned with X GPUs (we need infra to size exact instance count). This would come with a ~15% pricing uplift and capacity reservation.

Action items:
- Jonas: can you confirm the Dedicated sizing & uplift estimate and add a short note on measurement instrumentation (what metric we will publish back to Nimbus)?
- Stephanie: please draft a customer-facing options table (A: hosted carveout w/ fallback; B: Dedicated SLA + pricing).
- Legal/Contracts will need to own language on "fallback" and measurement windows (30-day rolling, p95).

I am happy to present either option to Marcus. If we go hosted carveout, we should be conservative so we can deliver.

— Mina

(Forwarded attachments: nimbus-metrics-sample.csv, procurement-terms.pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Li <marcus.li@nimbus.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-14T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for streaming TTFT and sustained token/sec guarantees

Marcus — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Below are two concrete options we can provide; pick the one that best fits Nimbus's risk appetite and procurement timeline.

Option 1 — Hosted carveout (fastest to deploy)
- Coverage: us-west region only
- Measurement: 30-day rolling window, p95 computed per-client per-minute, aggregated across the account
- TTFT guarantee (streaming): p95 <= 200 ms
- Sustained token/sec: not guaranteed; we provide monitoring and a "best-effort" target of 35 tokens/sec per concurrent stream.
- Fallback: in overload, we will route to a compatible quantized variant and/or alternate region; fallback behavior and notification hooks documented in appendix.
- Commercial: no dedicated commit; standard hosted rates apply.

Option 2 — Dedicated SLA (higher assurance)
- Coverage: customer-dedicated pool; global routing per policy
- Measurement: 30-day rolling, p95 per stream
- TTFT guarantee (streaming): p95 <= 150 ms
- Sustained token/sec guarantee: >= 50 tokens/sec per concurrent stream (for streams > 10k tokens)
- Commit & pricing: Dedicated instance(s) as sized by Redwood infra. Estimated uplift: ~15% above standard Dedicated baseline (Jonas to confirm exact quote).
- Commercial: requires a 12-month reserved capacity commit + mutual action plan.

Next steps we propose:
1) If Nimbus wants the Hosted carveout, Redwood will issue a short SLA-exception letter (we'll finalize language with Legal). We will run a 14-day verification pilot to validate TTFT and throughput metrics against Nimbus traffic.
2) If Nimbus prefers Dedicated, Jonas will provide the sizing + formal quote and we will attach the Dedicated SLA to the order form.

I attached an updated SLA-exception-proposal (final draft) and a short checklist for the pilot. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday 11/20 to decide? If you want, we can have Infra join to walk the measurement instrumentation.

Thanks — Stephanie

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: SLA-exception-proposal-ND-2025.pdf (final), pilot-checklist.md (txt)
